extracted.intended_audience: recording artists, songwriters, producers, engineers, Recording Academy members, and music industry professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Updated Rules & Guidelines for the GRAMMY Awards (64th GRAMMY Awards / changes affecting eligibility, category definitions, award recipient limits, anti-manipulation policies, and technical award rules). Useful for anyone submitting recordings or participating in GRAMMY voting/awards processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Of The Year — Nominee and Recipient Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Moving forward, all credited artists (including featured artists), songwriters of new material, producers, recording engineers, mixers, and mastering engineers are eligible to be GRAMMY nominees and recipients in the Album Of The Year category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously the rule stated that all artists, songwriters, producers, recording engineers, mixers, and mastering engineers were required to be credited with at least 33 percent or more of playing time. That 33% playing-time threshold has been removed; eligibility now depends on being credited (including featured artists) or being a songwriter of new material. Change goes into effect immediately for the 64th GRAMMY Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dance/Electronic Recording — category definition and screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The category formerly known as 'Best Dance Recording' has been renamed 'Best Dance/Electronic Recording.' This category is intended for recordings with significant electronic-based instrumentation generally based around a rhythmic dance beat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening criteria include established dance and electronic recording genres as well as related emerging genres in order to accurately reflect current trends in dance and/or electronic music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical Field — singles eligible in five classical categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Singles that are not part of an album will now be eligible in five Classical categories: Best Orchestral Performance, Best Choral Performance, Best Chamber Music/Small Ensemble Performance, Best Classical Instrumental Solo, and Best Contemporary Classical Composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change implemented to reflect trends in classical music consumption; singles (standalone tracks) may be submitted/considered in these specified categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music For Visual Media — compilation category award limits (pre-existing masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: For albums consisting largely of pre-existing masters, up to two album producers and up to two music supervisors can be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets clearer limits on the number of participants who can be awarded in the Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media category when the album is largely assembled from pre-existing masters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music For Visual Media — award limits for largely new recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: For albums consisting largely of new recordings, principal artist(s) with significant contributing performance(s) (ensemble-driven casts in which performers have comparable musical and dramatic participation in the recording are not eligible); up to three producer(s) (in extraordinary circumstances an appeal for a possible fourth will be considered); and up to two music supervisors can be awarded. An engineer/mixer(s) who contributes greater than 50 percent playing time of newly recorded material can also be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who may be named recipients on albums of new recordings for visual media. Ensemble casts with comparable participation are excluded from principal-artist eligibility. Producers and music supervisor award counts are capped, with a narrow path for an additional producer by appeal. Engineer/mixer eligibility is tied to contributing >50% playing time of newly recorded material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music For Visual Media — timing/eligibility option for works tied to later-released visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Albums and tracks released during the current eligibility period that are associated with a visual medium releasing in the next eligibility period have two submission options: (1) enter during the current year in categories that are not in the Music For Visual Media Field (but they will not be eligible the following year in the Music For Visual Media Field if this option is chosen); or (2) enter them the following year as long as they do not get entered in any category during the current year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entering in the following year, albums will only be eligible in their respective category: Compilation or Score. Songs will be eligible in Song Written For Visual Media and may also be eligible in other song categories if they meet the 'track from a previous year is eligible' rule. This gives entrants a choice to avoid being locked out of Music For Visual Media eligibility when the associated visual release is delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Film Field — eligibility clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Music-related documentaries must contain a minimum of 51 percent of performance-based material or individual music videos that together create a visual album (if videos are packaged and entered together as one cohesive film).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic feature films and biopics are not eligible for the Music Film Field, while films with fictional elements are eligible. The 51% performance-based-material threshold is the quantitative test for documentary eligibility; packaged music-video albums are treated as cohesive films if entered as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical GRAMMY — new organization/company award
rubrics_metrics.description: A second Technical GRAMMY Award has been added, specifically reserved for a company, organization or institution. This award would be optional, and at the yearly discretion of the Technical GRAMMY Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an organizational-level Technical GRAMMY in addition to awards for individuals. The committee has yearly discretion whether to present it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical GRAMMY — individual award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Technical GRAMMY is awarded to those individuals who have dramatically pushed boundaries and made groundbreaking, important, outstanding, and influential contributions of technical excellence and innovation to the recording field throughout their lifetime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the qualitative standards used to evaluate lifetime technical contributions (innovation, influence, technical excellence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote trading and manipulation restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Academy members or their designated publicists are now restricted to FYC emails, social media posts and physical mailings that promote only their own recordings, prohibiting lobbying on behalf of other members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy prohibits promotion/lobbying on behalf of other members (vote trading or advocacy for others) via FYC communications and related promotional channels; communications must promote only the sender's own recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album eligibility — 'newly recorded' threshold raised to >75% playing time
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for GRAMMY Award consideration, an album must contain greater than 75 percent playing time of newly recorded (within five years of the release date), previously unreleased recordings. The current eligibility rule is 50 percent; this updated rule goes into effect for the 65th GRAMMY Awards (2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the quantitative threshold (>75% of playing time) and the definition window for 'newly recorded' (within five years of the release date). Note exceptions: Best Compilation Soundtrack, Best Historical Album, Best Immersive Audio Album, Best Recording Package, Best Special Package, and Best Album Notes accept albums of recordings that are not newly recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to album 'newly recorded' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories accept albums of recordings that are not newly recorded: Best Compilation Soundtrack, Best Historical Album, Best Immersive Audio Album, Best Recording Package, Best Special Package, and Best Album Notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicitly carved out from the general album eligibility 'newly recorded' requirement and may be submitted even if the album does not meet the >75% newly recorded threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of nomination review committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously announced change: discontinuation of nomination review committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as part of earlier April changes; indicates that nomination review committees (which had previously been part of the nomination/selection process) have been discontinued to increase transparency. No detailed procedures provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction in number of categories in which voters may vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously announced change: reduction in the number of categories in which voters may cast votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy change (announced in April) restricts how many categories individual voters may vote in, intended to focus voting scope; the page references this as part of prior amendments but does not provide the numeric limit on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of new categories (Best Global Music Performance; Best Música Urbana Album)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously announced addition of categories including Best Global Music Performance and Best Música Urbana Album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among earlier announced changes — new categories reflect diversification and recognition of global and genre-specific music; the page references these additions but does not include their full category rules here.
